One of you was too much.|[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] to [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Ozrei N'takkilomandrife]]|<ref name="Star Wars (1977) 95">[[Star Wars (1977) 95|''Star Wars'' (1977) 95]]</ref>}}
The '''Nagai''', {{Pronounced|nɑ'gɑi}}, also called the '''N'Gai''' and the '''Knives''', were a [[Near-Human|near-human]] [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] from [[Nagi/Legends|Nagi]], a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in the dwarf [[Satellite/Legends|satellite]] [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] called [[Firefist]] orbiting the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic disk]] in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]].

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Nagai_telepath.jpg|thumb|left|150px|A Nagai telepath]]
The Nagai were tall and thin [[near-Human]]s with pale skin, jet-black hair, gray eyes, and angular features.<ref name="UAA" /><ref name="LECG" /> Considered attractive, yet gaunt and frail looking by galactic standards, they were aware of the
effect their appearance had on others, and often allowed others to see them as weak until the time was right to reveal their true skills. Possessing lightning fast reflexes, the Nagai were known for their speed and agility in and out of combat, with much of their clothing, like traditional [[Electromesh]] armor, being tailored around their natural dexterity.<ref name="UAA" />

Nagai were noted as being especially charismatic; a quality that was by and large the product of their enhanced vocal range, allowing them to modulate and tailor their speech.<ref name="LECG" /> Described as incredibly soothing and hypnotic, a Nagai could use their voice to influence other sentient beings - provided their voice could be heard, and their words understood.<ref name="UAA" />

Despite their ubiquitous reputation as pale specters, Nagai were well known for their individualistic expression, with clothing and hair styles varying wildly from individual to individual depending on personal tastes and the image that a Nagai wanted to convey.<ref name="UAA" /><ref name="LECG" />

==Society and culture==
Intense, focused, and highly disciplined warriors, the Nagai were known to kill without hesitation if it suited them, particularly if honor demanded it,<ref name="UAA" /> and were reputed to fear nothing, aside from losing their own freedom.<ref name="LECG" /> If there was no honor in killing, or if their foe was weak, they took no pleasure in the victory.<ref name="UAA" /> Honor was everything to a Nagai; if a Nagai's honor was stripped away, whether forcefully or unknowingly, the Nagai had to take his own life. If the Nagai failed to do so, then it was the duty of others to fulfill that honor. As passionate in loving as they were in killing, a Nagai's honor told them that devotion to one's lover was the most important devotion one could ever offer, even if that devotion was unreturned.<ref name="Gamer">{{GamerCite|1|The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life: The Marvel Series}}</ref> Beyond this devotion, however, Nagai had little concern for individuals outside of their own families, only aiding others when bound by honor or seeking personal gain.<ref name="LECG" /><ref name="UAA" />

Despite the high esteem that honor held in their daily lives, Nagai could be found in a broad range of professions across the galaxy, ranging from traditional roles such as [[Noble/Legends|nobles]] and [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] to the more streetwise vocations of [[Scoundrel/Legends|scoundrels]] and [[Thief/Legends|thieves]].<ref name="LECG" /><ref name="UAA" />

Highly competent duelists, melee combat&mdash;especially the use of edged weaponry&mdash;was highly integrated into Nagai culture, with it being rare for a Nagai to not display expert use in blades of all sizes.<ref name="LECG" /> Particularly, skill with traditional [[Tehk'la blade]]s, [[Longsword/Legends|longswords]], and [[Swiftcut foil]]s were prized - the weapons being employed in a number of fighting exercises that were daily customs in Nagai society. These exercises were both a form of [[Meditation/Legends|meditation]] and a sign of social status; success and skill in wielding them in duels was the primary means of ascension through societal ranks, though many customs of daily life involved exercises with those weapons.<ref name="Gamer" />

In addition to martial ability, Nagai possessed a bizarre&mdash;and some would say cruel&mdash;sense of humor borne from generations of adversity under the [[Tof/Legends|Tof]].<ref name="LECG" /><ref name="UAA" /> Nagai duelists would often employ that wit in battle which, when coupled with their charisma, often set opponents off-balance.<ref name="LECG" /><ref name="UAA" />

==Technology==
Nagai technology was advanced. While their ships defied common design sense, they were nonetheless capable of far greater speed and efficiency than most [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] vessels. Nagai weapons technology, especially [[Sonic weapon/Legends|sonic weaponry]] was highly advanced, with the [[Kob sonic blaster|Nagai sonic blaster]] being able to rend flesh at the molecular level, though many Nagai officers felt it to be a dishonorable weapon to use in a fight. Nagai also made extensive use of [[Electromesh]] armor, improving on its basic design, and made significant advances in [[Cloaking device/Legends|cloaking technology]].<ref name="Gamer" />

==Politics==
Before the [[Tof/Legends|Tofs]] invaded, Nagai society was comprised of a caste system consisting of a series of [[Circle (Nagai)|Circles]], which were broken down into a series of sub-circles. An individual's place in the Circles was determined by birth, but it was possible to move up the ranks through tests of physical prowess. During the [[Tof/Legends|Tof]] invasions, this system broke down as Circles intermeshed for survival purposes. With many Sub-circles eradicated by the [[Tof/Legends|Tofs]], many lower levels moved up by default, and began mating with those previously above them; as a result, the entire system of Circles was no longer considered the solid institution it once was, with some radical thinkers urging its abandonment.<ref name="Gamer" />

==History==
The Nagai were just developing superluminal travel when they encountered the [[Tof/Legends|Tofs]], who followed Nagai scoutships to their home system and promptly began an invasion. The Nagai fought back, waging guerrilla wars against their conquerors over centuries. To aid in their fight against the Tofs, the Nagai allied with a neighboring species, the [[Maccabree]], outfitting them with mechanical limbs for ground fighting. They also allied with the [[Faruun]] shipwrights for vessels of war. Slowly a pathological hatred and fear of the Tofs developed, intensified by the Tof conquest of their homeworld Nagi. This drove the Nagai and Maccabrees outward into the wider [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]], which they referred to as the ''Skyriver''. With the assistance of the Dark Lady [[Lumiya]], a plan was developed to use the resources of the ''Skyriver'' to mount a liberation of their homeworld, and shortly after the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] had exhausted both sides, the Nagai struck.

The Nagai attempted to restart the Wookiee slave trade on [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]]. They were originally known to the [[Alliance of Free Planets|Alliance]] as "Knives", due to the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] mispronunciation of an individual Nagai encountered there. As a result, they were encountered by the [[Alliance of Free Planets]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] to stop their actions.

After being stopped by [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], they regrouped with [[Lumiya]] and her faction of the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] in an attempt to destroy the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] and gain territory to re-establish themselves. After various skirmishes on [[Skirmish on Kabray|Kabray]], [[Skirmish on Kinooine|Kinooine]], and [[Battle of Mandalore (Nagai invasion)|Mandalore]], they attacked [[Endor/Legends|Endor]]. With the aid of an [[Bey|inside agent]], they learned all of the Alliance dogfighting maneuvers and were able to easily outfight them at first. Once the Rebels caught on, though, the tables turned, and they were driven off the moon.

The Nagai continued invading a number of other planets with their allies, such as [[Battle of Iskalon (Nagai–Tof War)|Iskalon]]. Discovering a Tof force on the planet [[Trenwyth/Legends|Trenwyth]], they attempted to wipe them out but were [[Battle of Trenwyth|defeated]] there. Launching an [[Battle of Zeltros|attack on Zeltros]], the [[Tof/Legends|Tofs]] made themselves known. The Nagai's fear and hatred of the Tofs enabled them to form an unlikely alliance with the Rebels and Imperials to combat them. Repelling the Tofs from [[Zeltros/Legends|Zeltros]], they signed a treaty with the Alliance and later ambushed the Tof crown prince at the planet [[Saijo/Legends|Saijo]] and forced the Tofs to surrender, thus ending the Nagai/Tof threat to the galaxy.

After the surrender, the Nagai were given Saijo to settle on. Only a few did so, joining the Alliance; the others (accompanied by the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]]) went to liberate Nagi from the Tofs. Their attempt to free the planet was ultimately successful.<ref name="LECG" /> [[File:Nagai-TURcov.png|thumb|right|200px|A Nagai male]]

==Nagai in the galaxy==
[[Gharn]] was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] Nagai [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] who served the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] on [[Taris/Legends|Taris]] during the [[Mandalorian Wars]].<ref name="Taris">{{KOTORbackups|0}}</ref>

[[Darth Nihl]] was a high-ranking Nagai [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] in [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire]] many millennia later.<ref name="LECG" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Nagai were created by writer [[Mary Jo Duffy]] and artist [[Cynthia Martin]]. Martin came up with the visual design by looking at anime, and also drew inspiration from a Japanese comic about a tragic vampire - which, according to Martin, had a strong influence on her concept drawings.<ref name="SWArchive-The Circle is Now Complete: Classic Marvel Talents - Cynthia Martin">{{SWArchive|url=eu/lit/comics/f20020718/index.html|text=The Circle is Now Complete: Classic Marvel Talents}}</ref>
